stories.headline: Hot October CPI Puts a December Fed Rate Hike in Play
stories.dek: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above forecasts, and Fed officials are openly discussing a quarter-point or half-point increase on Dec. 9.
pole_a_bullets: October payrolls rose 165,000 against a consensus near 59,000, with 84,000 jobs added in upward revisions. Bulls read that as an economy that can absorb higher rates.
Unemployment fell to 4.1% even as 421,000 people entered the labor force. Participation is rising alongside hiring.
Hikes by the Fed signal that it is acting against inflation. Bulls argue that credibility lowers the odds of a deeper downturn later.
Monthly CPI slowed from 0.6% in September to 0.4%. Bulls see a trend that is moving toward the Fed's goal, not away from it.
pole_b_bullets: Prices are rising faster than pay, according to CNN's reading of the data. Bears say household purchasing power is shrinking.
Hikes make borrowing costlier for households already stretched. Bank of America warned the October hold looks like a policy mistake and a half-point move is possible.
Under the strong headline, U-6 unemployment rose to 7.9% from 7.6%. Average unemployment duration hit 27.1 weeks, the highest since September 2021.
Stocks fell on Nov. 10 as traders priced in tighter policy, and Fed officials suggested hikes could continue into 2027. Bears see rising risk to equities and growth.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by strategists such as Edward Jones's Angelo Kourkafas, who called the jobs report a blowout, and by Fed officials favoring firm tightening.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by consumer-finance and housing-market commentators, and by analysts such as Bank of America's rates team.
evidence_left: BLS data reported Nov. 10: October CPI rose 0.4% against the 0.3% forecast, and core CPI rose 0.3% (CNBC, Benzinga). No annual rate was published, because October 2025 prices were never collected during the shutdown.
The Fed held rates at 3.75%-4% in October after a quarter-point hike in September (The Hill, CNN). The December meeting is Dec. 8-9.
evidence_right: Governor Waller said he leans toward a 25 basis point hike and that 50 should be considered. Dallas Fed President Logan called for at least two more 25-point hikes (CNBC, Bloomberg). CME FedWatch put half-point odds at 13.6% (CNBC).
October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment was 4.1% (BLS via SHRM, Fidelity). Forecasts differed: Fidelity cited a 59,000 consensus and AP cited 65,000.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNBC, CNN, Reuters via Yahoo Finance, SHRM (BLS data), November 15, 2026.

stories.headline: White House Warns Incoming House Democrats That Probes Could Be Criminal
stories.dek: A letter from the White House counsel to the likely Oversight chair previews a legal fight over investigations of the Trump administration.
pole_a_bullets: Congressional oversight has limits. Supporters of the letter say probes that are partisan or exceed legitimate legislative purposes can break the law.
Any administration is entitled to prepare legal defenses and to contest subpoenas it considers overbroad. Hiring counsel's-office staff is routine preparation.
Past Republican-led probes of the Biden era drew accusations of partisanship. Conservatives say both parties use oversight as a political weapon.
Presidents need confidential executive-branch deliberations protected. Supporters see pushback as protecting the separation of powers.
pole_b_bullets: Article I of the Constitution gives Congress oversight power. Democrats say it does not depend on White House permission.
Threatening to investigate the investigators is intimidation, critics argue, and could chill legitimate inquiries.
Voters gave Democrats the House in the midterms. Democrats say oversight of the executive is a core duty of the majority.
Hiring 15 more lawyers and planning to resist subpoenas shows the administration expects scrutiny. Critics say that points to a need for transparency, not obstruction.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Trump administration officials and conservative legal commentators.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by House Democrats such as incoming Oversight Chair Robert Garcia, and by civil-liberties and government-accountability advocates.
evidence_left: White House counsel Will Scharf wrote to Rep. Robert Garcia, the likely incoming Oversight chair. The letter said aggressive probes may cross the line into blatant criminality (PBS/AP, The Hill). The Hill said Punchbowl News first reported it.
The Washington Post reported on Nov. 11 that the counsel's office has made 15 additional hires. It reported plans to resist subpoenas and to investigate the Democratic investigators.
evidence_right: Garcia said the Constitution gives Congress wide latitude to conduct investigations (NBC News).
AP reported voters dealt Trump and Republicans a defeat in the midterms. NBC projected Democrats would take control of the House.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NBC News, The Hill, PBS NewsHour, The Washington Post, November 15, 2026.

stories.headline: Huang's Resignation Revives Push to Tighten AI Chip Export Rules
stories.dek: Lawmakers of both parties want China chip limits added to the year-end defense bill after the Nvidia CEO stepped down amid spy-linked allegations.
pole_a_bullets: Huang has long argued that US firms must compete in the Chinese market. Industry voices say revenue from it funds the research that keeps the US ahead.
One executive's personal conduct does not show that existing export rules failed. Policy should rest on evidence about the chips, not on the scandal.
Location-verification mandates and broad bans written into a must-pass defense bill could be rushed. Critics warn of unintended costs for US chipmakers.
Cutting off China may push rivals to build alternatives and shrink US influence over global AI standards.
pole_b_bullets: Bipartisan lawmakers say the allegations show US chip policy is exposed to foreign intelligence. Rep. Mast said the scandal weakens Huang's lobbying against limits.
Sens. Warren and Coons asked for records on chip exports and Huang-Trump communications. They said the episode raises concerns about enforcement of export controls.
The Chip Security Act would require location verification on advanced chips. The AI Overwatch Act would restrict exports to countries of national-security concern.
Sen. Cornyn questioned why Huang received no FBI defensive briefing. Oversight supporters say agency processes need review.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Nvidia and chip-industry allies, and by export-control skeptics.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by China hawks in both parties, including Reps. Mast and Moolenaar, Sens. Banks and Warren, and Democratic leaders.
evidence_left: Nvidia's 8-K filing says CEO Jensen Huang resigned and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. PBS reported Huang left after reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. The Chinese government publicly denied engaging Alice Huang to spy on him (Axios).
Nvidia shares fell more than 4% at the Nov. 12 close (PBS). The Hill reported it is unclear whether the scandal will be enough to pass the chip bills.
evidence_right: House Speaker Mike Johnson told Politico he supports adding stronger chip export restrictions to the NDAA (VOA, Politico via Yahoo). Rep. Mast said they are very likely to be included (BigGo).
BigGo reported Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott asked Huang to testify Dec. 3. That detail is from a single outlet and not independently confirmed here.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NVIDIA 8-K (SEC), PBS NewsHour, The Hill, VOA News, November 15, 2026.
